rv.q: Mitchell's performance is the production's greatest strength.
Besides its quirky approach, Goblin is brutally sad and disturbed.
It is hard to be this funny while saying something this serious, and harder still to put the audience in a position that makes them feel almost responsible.
This wonderfully original production is both enormously entertaining and genuinely affecting.
Hilarious and heartbreakingly human, Goblin is a reminder to never judge your bitchy gay spin instructor.
All of this makes Goblin a unicorn of a play, rehashing an old premise and breathing new life into it through its sharp, honest, and occasionally original vision.

cn.t: Goblin earns strong notices for Derek Mitchell's seamless blend of comedy and heartbreak in this one-man show about teen loneliness and grooming. Most critics praise its emotional range, though some find the execution uneven.
